label: Bench our-way-prod GPS flake is grader-search variance plus terminate exit-code artifact not a daemon crash evidence chunk 1
title: Bench our-way-prod GPS flake is grader-search variance plus terminate exit-code artifact not a daemon crash evidence chunk 1
summary:
Investigated the agent-memory bench our-way-prod ON-arm flake (answers "I don't know" on the LongMemEval Oracle GPS probe; reported as "embedded daemon exits code=1 mid-drain" + "eager judge runs idle, candidates=[]"). Reproduced from the worktree (HEAD 00806352) with an embedded daemon live-bound to the conv workspace. Two findings:

(1) The "daemon exits code=1 mid-drain" is NOT a crash. bench/zonoid_bench/daemon.py stop() calls proc.terminate(), which on Windows is TerminateProcess -> exit code 1. The line "[daemon.py] daemon pid=X exited with code=1" is printed by stop() at teardown; piping interleaves stdout/stderr so it APPEARS mid-run. Verified: spawned pid == pidfile pid, /health=ready, Popen.poll()=None (alive) throughout the drain; only after stop() does returncode become 1. So failure (1) is a misread teardown artifact. The embedded daemon does not actually die mid-drain on this box.
